entries.sourceClaim: The slide labels (rmax−rmin)/2 a geometric center; it is a half-range, not a general midpoint.
entries.qualification: The midpoint is (20+80)/2=50, whereas (80−20)/2=30 is the half-width.

entries.sourceClaim: The bounded half-range formula cannot reach the >55 mood branch described on the same page.
entries.qualification: The largest interval width is 100, so half of it is at most 50.

entries.sourceClaim: The printed angular half-difference is not the angular midpoint, and circular angles additionally require wrap-aware treatment.
entries.qualification: The midpoint is (20+140)/2=80°, while the half-span is (140−20)/2=60°.

entries.sourceClaim: The phrase emotional balance can be mistaken for a universal human constraint; the rule is a deliberate artificial-state design.
entries.qualification: The complement rule defines this model; it does not establish a psychological law.

entries.sourceClaim: The notebook implements a centered vector sum, not the printed half-range formula on PDF page1573.
entries.qualification: The code sums centered signed vectors and uses their Euclidean resultant magnitude.

entries.sourceClaim: The notebook uses a centered magnitude below10, whereas the slide describes a45–55 band.
entries.qualification: The code marks a small centered resultant neutral using a strict radius threshold of10.

entries.sourceClaim: The notebook maps calmness to friendliness as an implementation choice; the concepts are not synonyms.
entries.qualification: The code deliberately uses calmness for one social-state axis; that choice needs evaluation and is not a universal equivalence.

entries.sourceClaim: The source comment says last12 turns, but the code keeps12 messages, equivalent to6 complete exchanges.
entries.qualification: Each call appends two messages, so the last12 message entries represent6 complete pairs.

entries.sourceClaim: Comments describe turns, but the sliced elements are individual role/content messages.
entries.qualification: These slices count the latest message dictionaries; they are3 and4 complete pairs under the normal paired history.

entries.sourceClaim: The success criterion is aspirational; the slide reports no validation result establishing achievement.
entries.qualification: A stated success criterion still requires an operational evaluation and evidence.

entries.sourceClaim: The flow loops through strategies after a box named Test FER Model; strategy selection must not silently consume the final independent test set.
entries.qualification: Validation supports model selection; a held-out test set estimates performance after that selection.

entries.sourceClaim: The statement full fine-tuning generally has the highest accuracy with enough data is conditional, not a universal ordering.
entries.qualification: Allowing more layers to adapt gives flexibility, but does not guarantee the best held-out result.

entries.sourceClaim: Page1580 shows Dense Output8, while page1582 presents a seven-label example; these are not silently the same task.
entries.qualification: An eight-output diagram cannot define a seven-class label mapping by itself; the task schema determines the output dimension.

entries.sourceClaim: The slide attributes a seven-item list including neutral to Ekman; that conflates a common classification label set with the theory’s list.
entries.qualification: The example includes neutral; Ekman’s seven-emotion list includes contempt instead, so the task label set and historical theory must be distinguished.

entries.sourceClaim: The slide says both measure energy levels and calls arousal calmness; valence is not energy, and arousal spans calm to activated.
entries.qualification: Valence and arousal describe different aspects of affect rather than two copies of physical image energy.

entries.sourceClaim: The outer axis labels on the slide are swapped relative to the plotted V/A annotations; the question explicitly follows the numeric annotations.
entries.qualification: The printed V and A values vary across horizontal and vertical position respectively, contradicting the swapped outer labels.

entries.sourceClaim: The illustrative90% output is not accompanied by calibration or accuracy evidence.
entries.qualification: A displayed score needs validation and interpretation before it can support a calibrated probabilistic claim.

entries.sourceClaim: Multimodal fusion can improve robustness, but improvement and missing-channel tolerance are not automatic guarantees.
entries.qualification: Complementary inputs can help, but missing-modality robustness is a system property that must be tested.

entries.sourceClaim: The opening distinction can be read too absolutely; conversation-oriented use is the emphasis, not exclusive ownership of memory.
entries.qualification: The slide highlights a role in social interaction rather than a universal exclusion of memory from other robots.

additionalScope: No photographed person is diagnosed or assigned an internal mental state; only supplied annotations and model conventions are assessed.
The original deterministic engine cells were executed with synthetic inputs; live Ollama inference and interactive UI were not executed.
No package installation or model download was performed for L50.
Model-reported confidence is not established calibration.
The handwritten polar figure and the notebook use different angle layouts.
Feature reduction in the VGG illustration says Flatten/GlobAvPool; these are alternatives, not identical operations.
